etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English dime, from Anglo-Norman disme (“one tenth, tithe”) (modern French dîme), from Medieval Latin decima, from Latin decima (pars) (“tenth (part)”). Doublet of decim, decima, and decime.

definitions.definition: (US, Canada) A coin worth one-tenth of a dollar.
(Canada, US) A small amount of money.
(slang) A playing card with the rank of ten.

quote.citation: 2007 05, Ted McClelland, Horseplayers: Life at the Track, Chicago Review Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: At one point, Rob hit a dire losing streak. In a single week, he dropped a dime—$1,000.

definitions.definition: (slang) A measurement of illicit drugs (usually marijuana) sold in ten dollar bags.

quote.citation: 2007 September 23, David Bowman, “Torchlit Crit”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: These deaths got him a dime in a minimum-security prison.

definitions.definition: (US, slang) A beautiful woman (10 on a 10-point scale).

quote.citation: 2005, “Stay Fly”, in Jordan Houston, Darnell Carlton, Paul Beauregard, Premro Smith, Marlon Goodwin, David Brown, Willie Hutchinson (lyrics), Most Known Unknown‎[2], performed by Three 6 Mafia (featuring Young Buck, 8 Ball, and MJG), Sony BMG:
quote.text: Make a couple of nuns a couple of dimes.

quote.citation: 2008, “House Music”, in Afterparty Babies, performed by Cadence Weapon:
quote.text: Wait in line for drinks, it’s another time out / Made out on the floor with a couple dimes

definitions.definition: (American football) A defensive formation with six defensive backs, one of whom is a dimeback.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From the use of the coin in a payphone to report a crime to the police. US payphones charged 10¢ in almost all jurisdictions until the late 1970s.

definitions.definition: (US, slang, with "on") To inform on, to turn in to the authorities, to rat on, especially anonymously.
(US, slang) To operate an audio amplifier (especially an electric guitar amplifier) at level "10" (typically the highest amplification level).
